text.p: Oil and gas producer Woodside Petroleum Ltd is expected to unveil a 52 percent surge in profits for the six months to June 30 on the back of higher production and realised prices coupled with lower costs.
Analysts' average forecasts were for a net profit before abnormals of A$96.5 million, up from the A$63.3 million posted for the previous corresponding period.
Forecasts for Woodside's half year profit, due on Wednesday, ranged from A$91.7 million to A$102 million.

"Basically domestic gas has been pretty healthy and LNG is looking good too, but basically it's rising liquids production that's driving the increase in revenue and profitability," said ANZ Securities analyst Gordon Ramsay
Ramsay pegged his interim forecast at A$94 million.
Woodside has reported first half sales revenues totalling A$370 million or 28 percent higher than last year.
More than half of the year-on-year revenue growth came from LNG and crude oil production at the Wanaea/Cossack project offshore Western Australia which was commissioned in November last year.
However, during the half, potential production at the project was restricted by weather and technical problems.

The longest interruption, which deferred revenue to the project partners of about A$65 million, was from December 9 to February 19 caused by Tropical Cyclone Frank and subsequent mechanical failure on the floating production vessel.

The Wanaea and Cossack fields are part of the North West Shelf project which is an equal partnership between Woodside, The Broken Hill Pty Co, Chevron Corp, Japan Australia LNG(MIMI) Pty Ltd and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
Condensate earnings also were seen rising with the bringing on of more wells feeding into the Goodwyn platform.
"(Goodwyn) will start humming away so you'll get condensate volumes a little bit better as well," said one analyst.
Oil prices moved in Woodside's favour over the half with West Texas Intermediate rising to an average price US$20.50 a barrel from US$20.50 previously.
A complementary rise in the value of the Australian dollar was, however, unlikely to have put significant pressure on earnings.

"They've a lot of forwards they put in place at the end of last year at about US$0.7350. They're relatively desensitised against some of the volatility in the underlying Australian dollar oil price," said BT Securities analyst Stuart Baker
The company was seen extracting some interest cost savings due to lower global interest rates.
LIBOR averaged 5.4 percent over the half, compared with 6.2 percent a year ago, an analyst said.
